newsitem.title: UK: Euro shares hit by Wall St, political worries.
newsitem.headline: Euro shares hit by Wall St, political worries.

text.p: European bourses slipped in early trading on Friday, weighed down by a poor overnight close on Wall Street and a bout of jitters over political uncertainty.
On currency markets, the dollar was virtually unchanged against the yen despite fresh concern about the health of the Japanese financial system after the suspension of a big Japanese insurer.

London, Frankfurt and Paris got off to a dull beginning with investors clearly unsettled by New York's weaker bonds and stocks, which fell 20.47 points to 6,792.25 on Thursday on the Dow Jones industrial average.
"It's a damp start," said Charterhouse head of research, Richard Jeffrey, in London. "Wall Street was mildly off, we are still in the clutch of political uncertainty."

Many investors were sitting on the sidelines ahead of the May 1 general election in which the Conservative government is expected to be ousted by the oppostion Labour party, according to opinion polls.
"No one's going to set up fresh positions ahead of the weekend and we've seen just about all the catch up in the financials we're going to see," said one senior dealer.
Sharp gains in bank stocks this week have helped the main FTSE index up, with investors scrambling to increase weightings before further building society flotations.

The Paris bourse slipped in and out of profit in early trade but was showing a small loss by mid-morning in thin trading. Many investors were also holding back amid election uncertainty, traders said.

"Investors will steer clear until the election. The risk, in terms of market valuation, is too great. Better wait a month and find out what France's direction will be," said one trader. "Until then, we'll be driven by the polls."
An IPSOS poll showing the ruling conservative coalition would get a wafer-thin majority weighed on French financial markets on Thursday afternoon.
In Frankfurt, stocks fell a few points in floor trading and in computerised dealing as investors marked time after Wall Street's losses and on profit-taking before the weekend.
In currencies, the dollar was virtually unchanged from the levels seen in late European trade on Thursday.

The suspension of the big Japanese insurance company Nissan Mutual Life Insurance Company triggered concern that Nissan's foreign bonds would be liquidated, causing a large repatriation of funds and weakening the dollar.
But the dollar marked time and was not expected to move much before the weekend meeting of finance ministers and central bankers from the G7 group of industrialised countries in Washington.

"The latest worries about Japan's financial system are a distraction for the market ahead of the G7, and the yen is a touch stronger as a result but the FX impact was marginal," said Roger Francis, senior analyst at IBJ International.
The dollar was also supported against the yen by a comment from Bank of Japan governor Yasuo Matsushita who said the central bank was sticking to its easy monetary policy for the time being.
Traders will be keeping a close on eye on Friday's meeting in Washington between U.S. President Bill Clinton and Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto.

The contentious trade balance issue between the two countries was highlighted by an article in the The Washington Post, saying Clinton sent a blunt letter to Hashimoto warning that Tokyo's economic policies raised the risk of a dangerous surge in Japan's trade surplus.

Many traders expect the G7 to come out with a rehashed version of the statement released at its last meeting in Berlin in February when it said that that major misalignments in exchange markets had been corrected.
STOCKS AT 0930 GMT
London's FTSE 100 was down 3.5 points at 4,385.0.
The Paris CAC-40 index was down 1.96 points at 2,537.87.
Frankfurt's DAX index was down 19.93 at 3,377.43.
CURRENCIES AT 1000 GMT
The dollar stood at 1.7155 against the mark versus 1.7150 in late European trade on Thursday. Against the yen, the dollar was quoted at 125.87 from 125.90.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $341.35 an ounce after ending at $340.65 in London. Silver was at $4.73, one cent higher.
